models.name: Qwen 3.6 27B
models.description: Candidate for a side-by-side test against Qwen 3.5 27B on 24-32 GB GPUs; not an install default. It has the same architecture as Qwen 3.5 27B, so memory use and speed should match (about 21 GiB at 64K context). Qwen's own table scores it higher (Terminal-Bench 2.0 59.3 vs 41.6, SWE-bench Verified 77.2 vs 75.0), but those runs used thinking mode and ODS serves with reasoning off. Known risks: instruction following may be weaker, llama.cpp does not enforce tool_choice required for Qwen 3.6 with thinking off (#27767), and it repeated one tool call in a loop in 3 of 216 MMBT cells. No ODS app results yet.

publisher_evidence.note: Same-table publisher results with thinking-mode sampling (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95). ODS serves local models with LLAMA_ARG_REASONING=off, so read the deltas as direction, not size. The Qwen 3.6 27B card has no instruction-following row; the possible dip comes only from cross-table comparison (Qwen 3.5 27B card: IFBench 76.5), so exact-text behavior needs fleet evidence.

models.name: KAT-Coder V2.5 Dev 35B-A3B
models.description: Kuaishou's July 2026 SFT and RL post-train of Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B for repository-scale coding, tool discipline, and efficient agent loops. Independent 120-run evidence tied the best pass rate while using about half the stock models' input tokens.

quality_evidence.note: KAT tied the best of four 35B-class models at 29/30 passes, used 12.6M input tokens versus 25.1M for stock Qwen 3.6, and had zero malformed tool-call leaks in the cited research task. The study used the MTP-grafted APEX I-Balanced sibling; this 40-block artifact removes the grafted draft head and therefore requires its own fleet validation. The study also had one harness, one GPU, five repetitions per task, and a quantization confound favoring the post-trains.

publisher_evidence.note: Publisher-reproduced results use disclosed 256K agent harnesses and one run per evaluation. They are supporting evidence, not a substitute for fleet validation or independent reruns.

source_evidence.license_note: The KAT checkpoint is Apache-2.0 licensed; commercial use, modification, and redistribution are permitted subject to license notice and attribution requirements.
source_evidence.gguf_metadata_note: The exact artifact reports qwen35moe, 256 experts with 8 active, 262K native context, and 40 model blocks with no grafted MTP draft layer. It embeds the upstream pre-fix chat template (SHA-256 e84f32a23fdda27689f868aa4a1a5621f41133e51a48d7f3efcbea2839574259), which rejects non-leading system messages; upstream fixed that template at revision 3a7d874090df0cd4399401982eca67df2c5a7e82, so exact deployed-consumer validation is required before recommendation.

rejected_artifacts.reason: The grafted 41st MTP block requires llama.cpp MTP loader support merged after the ODS production builds. ODS llama.cpp b8668 on Strix Halo/ROCm and b9014 on Tower2/CUDA both interpreted it as a normal hybrid block and failed with missing tensor 'blk.40.ssm_conv1d.weight' despite ample memory.
